import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 566

*References*:
- [erdosproblems.com/566](https://www.erdosproblems.com/566)
- [EFRS93] Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, _Ramsey size linear graphs_.
Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 389-399.
-/

namespace Erdos566

open SimpleGraph

/--
Let $G$ be such that any subgraph on $k$ vertices has at most $2k-3$ edges.
Is it true that, if $H$ has $m$ edges and no isolated vertices, then $R(G,H) \ll m$?

In other words: if $G$ is sparse (every induced subgraph on $k$ vertices has $≤ 2k-3$ edges),
is $G$ Ramsey size linear?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_566 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (p : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin p)),
      (∀ S : Finset (Fin p), 2 ≤ S.card → (G.induce S).edgeSet.ncard ≤ 2 * S.card - 3) →
      G.IsRamseySizeLinear := by
  sorry

end Erdos566

reformulations.difference: Lean tests the sparsity bound on induced graphs G[S], whereas the source states the bound for all subgraphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every subgraph F with vertex set S has at most as many edges as G[S], with the same number of vertices. Thus the bound for induced subgraphs implies the bound for arbitrary subgraphs. Conversely, every induced subgraph is a subgraph. Finsets enumerate all vertex subsets because the ambient vertex type is finite. Both the sparsity-condition equivalence and the resulting full conjecture equivalence were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: The sole declaration is faithful. IsRamseySizeLinear uses the ordinary vertex Ramsey number and a positive constant depending on G but uniform over H, with positive degree exactly excluding isolated vertices. Finite vertex types prevent ncard's infinite-set default, and finite Ramsey theory ensures the defining infimum is over a nonempty set. Scratch proofs verified the integer interpretation of 2*k-3 for k≥2, zero Ramsey numbers when either graph has no vertices, and harmless empty/singleton G cases. A graph H with no isolated vertices and zero edges necessarily has zero vertices. Computable sparsity tests accepted K0 through K3 and K4 minus an edge, and rejected K4. The source records OPEN, matching the category. The EFRS93 full PDF was unavailable; the publisher abstract and exact statement in the linked UCSD collection sufficed to settle this declaration.
